## In progress

- `2.4.1.1` Exclusive writer lock (`flock`) with clear error when held (M2)
- `2.4.1.2` Read-only open mode (also when rocompat flags unknown) (M2)
- `2.4.2` Append frames with group-fsync API (`append`, `sync`) (M2)
- `2.4.3.1` [T] crash simulation: fail after each step 1/2/3, reopen, assert previous or new commit visible, never partial (M2)
- `2.4.4.1` Choose superblock, scan from `log_end`, truncate torn tail (M2)
- `2.4.4.2` [T] an invalid frame in `wal_start..log_end` is `Corrupt` and never truncated; creating a container never truncates an existing file (SPEC §4.7, §8.6) (M2)
- `2.4.7` Fuzz target: arbitrary bytes as container → open must return `Err` or valid, never panic (M2)
- `2.4.9` Define `frame_seq` (SPEC §4.4): what it numbers, its first value after a rewrite, and whether recovery stops at a non-increasing one (M2)

## Ready next (first 15 todo leaves whose milestone deps are done)

- `2.3.6` Mapped reads of committed container ranges via `MmapFile` (SPEC §4.7, ADR-0010; needs 2.4.4: the mappable `log_end` comes from the container superblock, so it lands with 2.4): opt-in, or automatic only on local disk filesystems; `pread` fallback otherwise; mapping granularity (per frame vs `log_end` window); the only `unsafe` call site outside `persia-format` (M2)
- `2.3.8` Sweep stale `@tmp.*` files a crashed writer left (ADR-0012): which process may delete them (pid no longer running, or age), and when (open, or a `persia` CLI command) (M2)
- `2.3.9` `windows-latest` CI job for `persia-storage` (found in the 2.3 review): the `cfg(windows)` code (positioned reads, reserved names) is otherwise never compiled; directory fsync on Windows is 2.4.8 (M2)
- `2.4.5.1` Dead-space accounting (M2)
- `2.4.5.2` [T] crash during compaction leaves a valid old or new file (M2)
- `2.4.5.3` Windows: test whether an open mapping blocks `rename` over the container; if so, close mappings or defer the swap until readers drain (ADR-0010) (M2)
- `2.4.6` Expose logical objects (Segment/Manifest/WalChunk) via the `Storage` trait view for the engine (M2)
- `2.4.8` Platform notes: fsync semantics on macOS (`F_FULLFSYNC`), Windows (`FlushFileBuffers`), documented + tested where possible (M2)
- `2.4.10` Read-write open after a scan ends in corruption (SPEC §4.4): keep the bytes after the stop offset (quarantine copy or explicit repair flag) instead of truncating them; distinguish acknowledged WAL frames via 2.4.9 (ADR-0013: a valid frame past the stop whose `frame_seq` is not above the last valid one can never be acknowledged data, e.g. stale blocks exposed by a crash during a file extension; decide whether "only such frames and zeros" may be truncated) (M2)
- `2.4.11.1` A file-system shim under the 2.3 backend and the container adapter that can fail or drop `fsync`, lose a `rename` or directory entry while the data survives (or the reverse), and tear the tail of an append (M2)
- `2.4.11.2` [T] crash at every fsync point of 2.3.1 (temp → fsync → rename → fsync dir) and of the commit sequence (SPEC §4.5, §8): recovery yields the old or the new state, never a mix (M2)
- `2.5.1` `docker-compose.dev.yml` skeleton (MinIO, fake-gcs-server, Azurite — filled in M12), pinned image digests (M2)
- `3.1.1` Field types enum + per-field options (analyzer, boost, positions, k1, b, facet, stored) (M3)
- `3.1.2.1` Schema JSON (de)serialization with strict unknown-key rejection (M3)
- `3.1.2.2` Canonical encoding + schema hash (stable across versions) (M3)
